scientific_hypothesis: Starting from quarter-wave optical thickness seeds at band centers (375nm UV, 1350nm SWIR) with ±15% random jitter will escape local minima that constrained the chirped parameterization, while expanding thickness bounds to 500nm provides additional design freedom without violating fabrication limits.
expected_advantages: Better convergence than monotonicity-constrained chirp due to unconstrained thickness space
Quarter-wave seeds provide physically meaningful starting point
Expanded bounds allow thicker layers for broader UV reflection band
known_risks: May converge to local minimum if jitter amplitude insufficient
30 independent variables may require more optimization iterations
No monotonicity constraint could produce non-fabricable thickness profiles
expected_observations: valid_candidates should increase from 9 (route_01) to >= 15 if initialization reduces boundary collisions
best_target_score should remain >= 0.53 or improve if quarter-wave seed is closer to optimum
tightest_margin should not decrease across rounds if constraint set remains feasible
If valid_candidates remains < 10, hypothesis that initialization causes boundary collisions is falsified
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to route_01 historical best (0.5346) is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge search as stagnated -> stop and retain current best
If valid_candidates = 0, judge constraint set infeasible -> should relax thickness bounds, not re-run same route
If best_target_score exceeds 0.75, judge dual-band objective achievable -> can proceed to robustness analysis
